title: Building a library of physical work for robots.
standfirst: KinesthetiQ, founded by Prakhar Goel in Bengaluru, collects data on physical interaction, from robots at work and from real-world activity, so that robots have something to learn from. Its premise is that general-purpose robotics depends on large amounts of real-world interaction data.

hero.alt: Engineers reviewing a robotic arm test on a laptop at ARTPARK
hero.caption: Engineers testing a robotic arm at ARTPARK. ARTPARK photograph, not of KinesthetiQ.

lead: On KinesthetiQ’s website, dozens of short clips sit side by side. Many show someone operating robot arms: in a lab, in a supermarket aisle, in a washroom, in an office.
The clips are data collection. The company’s stated goal is a natural internet of physical interactions, from which robots can learn and improve. It is part of ARTPARK’s startup portfolio.

quote.text: Language models learned from the internet. Robots have no internet of physical work to learn from yet. We are building that library, one recorded interaction at a time.

blocks: KinesthetiQ calls its platform Physical Data Harvesting. It captures raw data from robotic operations and from real-world activities, then organises it with common protocols and tools for search and sharing. The company describes several ways of gathering it: gamification, networks of collection in the wild, and robot skill training centres across India.

figure.alt: A top camera view of a two-armed robot setup over a table with a bottle, cups and a cloth, above two wrist-camera views of orange textured grippers
figure.caption: One recording, three views: a camera above a two-armed robot setup, and a camera on each wrist. Video still from KinesthetiQ.

blocks: Prakhar has described the idea in a video titled Digitization of Physical Interactions. The website says pre-orders are open.

The company was incorporated on 30 May 2024 as Kinesthetiq Robotics Studio Private Limited. It is hiring a full stack roboticist in Bengaluru, to work on robotic systems end to end, across mechatronics, embedded systems and AI.
KinesthetiQ has not yet published a founder interview or a funding announcement.
